text:
Marco Diaz: Quick heads-up — Vectorium wants an EAP kickoff next week. They sent a redline NDA and a short list of bench asks: power, tail-latency, and inference stability under burst.
Tess Nguyen: I can coordinate the infra side. Which lab window are they thinking?
SI-Partner-Bot: Partner proposed 2026-06-10 to 2026-06-12, mornings PT. They also requested that any marketplace listing be held until after mutual approval.
Marco Diaz: OK hold on marketing + marketplace. @LegalBot please review their NDA redline, especially telemetry and publication clauses.
LegalBot: Reviewing now. Key flag: partner removed our right to retain telemetry for debugging. Also added a non-disparagement clause. Recommend we counter with 60-day telemetry retention and carve-outs for safety/incident investigations.
Ava Kaur: For benchmarks I suggest: p50/p95/p99, tail-loss rate, batch scaling (1..32), and a 1-hour soak with randomized request pacing. Models: redwood/base-3b, redwood/opt-7b, and a 4-bit quantized baseline.
Tess Nguyen: Add sequence sweep 64/256/1024. We'll need their perf counters (aggregated) and platform power traces. They said they can only provide anonymized traces w/ host masks. Is that OK?
Marco Diaz: Anonymized aggregated traces are fine. We cannot publish raw host identifiers or clock/power per core. Document that in runbook.
BenchBot: Proposed run job created: 2026-06-11T15:00Z. See config snippet below.
BenchBot: ```
models: redwood/base-3b,redwood/opt-7b
quant: 4bit
batches: 1,4,8,16,32
seq: 64,256,1024
profile: kvcache,mem,power,latency
soak: 3600s
random_load: true
```
Ava Kaur: We'll also capture KV-cache warmup curves and flamegraphs. Add `--capture-flamegraph true` flag.
Tess Nguyen: I will confirm RDMA and S3 reachability tonight. If partner provides encrypted perf bundles, we need instructions for ingest.
SI-Partner-Bot: Partner: "We will export aggregated perf bundles as gzipped tar with SHA256. We cannot export raw host-level traces or per-core clocks."
Marco Diaz: Noted. @LegalBot confirm that the data handling steps comply with the NDA redline.
LegalBot: Yes, provided we add an approved ingest flow and access control note. Also insist on a 30-day embargo on any public mention unless partner explicitly approves copy.
Ava Kaur: Can we get a kernel/driver version matrix from them? Small driver tweaks may affect latency.
SI-Partner-Bot: Partner will share driver versions and supported firmware list, but will not allow driver patches in their lab. They prefer we run on their validated stack, or a dedicated node image.
Tess Nguyen: We'll prepare both: validated-stack run plus a canary with our optimized kernel flagged as `--opt-kernel=false|true` so partner can approve later.
BenchBot: Scheduled canary window: 2026-06-10T16:00Z. Main run: 2026-06-11T15:00Z.
Marco Diaz: Marketing and PR: hold all messaging. No partner name in any internal or external dashboards until countersign and marketing approval.
ReleaseBot: Noted. Marketplace sync blocked until partner signs the joint announcement SOW.
Ava Kaur: After run, propose 45-minute readout: go over tail-latency, P95 regressions, and perf anomalies. Prepare a concise findings doc + CSV attachments.
Tess Nguyen: I'll upload runbook and checklist here: https://redwood.share/runs/vectorium-eap-runbook.md — preflight, access creds, logging, expected deliverables.
Marco Diaz: Next steps: Legal to upload NDA counter by EOD, Tess to confirm infra reachability, Ava to finalize bench config and scripts. Once NDA is signed we send partner the schedule.
Ava Kaur: I'll push the bench scripts to the run repo and tag `eap/vectorium/v1`. Drop any test vectors or load patterns in the repo by EOD.
LegalBot: Counter-NDA uploaded: https://redwood.share/nda/vectorium-counter-v1.pdf. Key changes: 60-day telemetry retention, embargo language, data ingestion controls.
SI-Partner-Bot: Partner acknowledged receipt. They will review and revert within 24-48 hours.
Marco Diaz: Great work team. Ping here if you need approvals fast. :thumbsup:
